title: Saint Francis and the Wolf of Gubbio
text:
According to The Little Flowers of Saint Francis, a huge wolf once terrorized the town of Gubbio in Umbria. It devoured animals and even people, and the townsfolk were so afraid that they went out armed, as if to war, and many would not leave the walls at all.

Francis, who was staying there, went out to find the wolf despite everyone's warnings. When it ran at him with open jaws, he made the sign of the cross and called it Brother Wolf. The wolf closed its mouth and lay down at his feet.

Francis spoke to it plainly. It had done great harm and deserved punishment, he said, but he wanted to make peace between it and the town. He knew it had done these things out of hunger. If the people promised to feed it every day, would it promise never to hurt man or beast again? The wolf bowed its head and placed its paw in his hand as a pledge.

Francis led it into the market square and repeated the pact before the whole town, and again the wolf gave its paw. For two years it lived in Gubbio, going from door to door and being fed, and the dogs did not even bark at it. When it died of old age, the people mourned it.
lesson: Many conflicts end only when you understand what is driving the other side and meet that need. A fair agreement, kept by both, can turn a threat into a neighbor.
people: Francis of Assisi, the wolf, the townspeople
source: The Little Flowers of Saint Francis (Fioretti), Chapter 21
caveat: The story is a legend first written down about 150 years after Francis's death.
